articles.body: Europe Offshore Operations Regulatory Renewables Polish offshore wind rules draw Danish shipowner backlash Adis Ajdin November 26, 2026 0 362 2 minutes read RWE RWE Danish shipowners have raised concerns at EU level over new Polish vessel certification requirements, warning that additional inspections are making it harder for foreign operators to compete for offshore wind and marine construction contracts in the Baltic Sea. Industry association Danish Shipping has challenged rules requiring certain foreign-flagged vessels below 500 gt to undergo additional technical surveys before working in Polish waters, even where they already hold certificates from their flag administrations. The requirements primarily affect crew transfer vessels (CTVs), which carry personnel and equipment to offshore wind farms, alongside smaller construction and support vessels. Under Poland’s revised Maritime Safety Act, foreign vessels not covered by the SOLAS convention that operate in relevant Polish waters for more than 14 days in a calendar year must obtain a national operating permit. The application process includes technical verification by a recognised organisation, adding costs and potentially taking vessels out of service while inspections are carried out. Danish Shipping argued that the additional procedures duplicate existing flag-state oversight and create obstacles for companies seeking work on Poland’s expanding offshore wind projects. Høj Nordic Marine Contractor, based in Horsens, is among the operators affected. Chief executive Michael Normann said the rules were restricting the company’s access to the Polish market despite its existing operating experience in the country. “The rules make it harder for us to bid for projects in Poland,” Normann said. The company warned that the additional certification procedures could limit vessel availability, increase project costs and complicate contractual commitments. Danish Shipping’s executive director for sustainable ships and skills, Nina Porst, questioned the need for a second approval process and warned that similar national requirements elsewhere in Europe could further complicate cross-border operations. The association has raised the matter at EU level, arguing that countries should recognise existing flag-state certification rather than impose additional national approval procedures. Poland’s changes were introduced through amendments adopted in October 2025. Polish maritime legal specialists have linked the measures to concerns about insufficient technical oversight of some foreign-flagged vessels operating outside the main international convention framework. The Maritime Office in Gdynia has published an operating-permit procedure requiring evidence that foreign vessels meet safety requirements no less stringent than those applying to Polish-flagged ships. Danish Shipping previously challenged similar requirements in Germany, which were withdrawn in December 2024 following industry objections. articles.title: UK offshore wind decommissioning estimates vary tenfold
articles.summary: Decommissioning provisions for UK offshore wind farms with similarly sized turbines can differ by as much as ten times, highlighting major uncertainties over the future cost of dismantling ageing installations, according to new research. A study by energy consultancy Xodus and its offshore renewables engineering arm...
articles.body: Europe Offshore Renewables UK offshore wind decommissioning estimates vary tenfold Bojan Lepic November 26, 2026 0 272 1 minute read Semco Maritime Semco Maritime Decommissioning provisions for UK offshore wind farms with similarly sized turbines can differ by as much as ten times, highlighting major uncertainties over the future cost of dismantling ageing installations, according to new research. A study by energy consultancy Xodus and its offshore renewables engineering arm Evolv Energies examined financial provisions disclosed by 37 operating UK offshore wind farms between 2019 and 2025, covering almost 2,500 turbines. The findings, published in a whitepaper titled Benchmarking Offshore Wind Decommissioning Provisions , revealed significant differences between projects. For turbines rated below 4 MW, reported provisions ranged from £180,000 ($236,000) to £1.83m ($2.4m) per turbine, while those above 8 MW ranged from £750,000 ($983,000) to £4.56m ($5.98m). Average provisions stood at approximately £900,000 ($1.18m) per turbine for smaller units and £1.5m ($1.97m) for the largest. The study also identified substantial changes over time, with one project’s estimated liability increasing more than sixfold during the review period, while others recorded only modest increases or downward revisions. Xodus said the variations suggest differences in engineering assumptions, removal requirements and accounting methods, making direct comparisons difficult. “Every offshore wind project is unique, and so we would expect decommissioning provisions to vary. What stands out, though, is the scale of this variation between projects using similar-sized turbines,” said Olivier Mette, head of advisory at Xodus. The findings come as Britain’s earliest offshore wind developments approach the end of their original design lives. Assuming a 25-year lifespan, 532 turbines included in the study will reach that milestone by 2036, rising to 1,285 by 2041. Operators will increasingly face decisions on whether to extend the life of existing installations, replace turbines or proceed with decommissioning. Xodus called for greater transparency in cost estimates and clearer regulatory guidance, particularly concerning requirements for restoring the seabed following removal. The consultancy stressed that reported provisions are discounted financial estimates, not definitive removal costs, and that existing offshore wind infrastructure could retain considerable value beyond its original design life. The sinking prompted Spain’s Directorate General of Merchant Marine to activate level two of its National Maritime Pollution Contingency Plan, with regional authorities also activating their civil protection arrangements. The tanker was carrying an estimated 7,000 tonnes of diesel, raising concerns about a possible spill in waters north of Ibiza. Initial inspections by the rescue vessel Guardamar Talía found no visible signs of pollution or floating wreckage. Spain has also deployed the specialist pollution-response ship Clara Campoamor , with aerial surveillance and satellite monitoring being arranged. The 120-m-long Med Emre , built in Turkey in 2019, is managed by Istanbul-based YMN Tanker Marine Management, while shipping databases show it operating for Spanish energy company Moeve. articles.body: Freire Shipyard Celebrates Launch of New Greenpeace Vessel Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 © Greenpeace International Freire Shipyard celebrated the launch ceremony of NB 737 on November 25, 2026 in Vigo, marking a milestone in the construction of Greenpeace International's new flagship vessel. Designed to support environmental campaigns and scientific research worldwide while minimizing fossil fuel consumption, the vessel is scheduled for delivery by the end of 2027. With an overall length of 75 meters, the new sailing vessel has been designed to undertake demanding, long-range maritime operations, including campaigns in polar regions. Its design prioritizes energy efficiency, combining wind propulsion with an intelligent energy generation, storage and management system to minimize fossil fuel consumption. The vessel will feature a range of energy generation and storage technologies, including solar panels, battery storage systems, energy recovery systems and hydrogen fuel cells. These will be complemented by four dual-fuel internal combustion engine generator sets for electricity generation designed to use green methanol (MeOH) as their primary fuel, with small quantities of marine gas oil (MGO) used to initiate combustion. One of the key features of the design is the automated DynaRig sailing propulsion system, comprising two rotating masts with a combined sail area of 1,746 square meters. Under favorable weather conditions, this configuration will enable the vessel to circumnavigate the globe using wind power alone. In addition, while sailing, the propellers will be able to operate as generators, harnessing the vessel's movement to produce electricity. The aim is for the vessel to operate with minimal fossil fuel use from the outset, with a view to eliminating it entirely as the necessary supply chains and infrastructure become available. In addition, the vessel will feature onboard laboratories, systems for deploying remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), a helideck equipped to support helicopter operations, and four auxiliary boats that can be deployed even in challenging sea conditions. With the addition of NB 737, Greenpeace will expand its fleet, which currently comprises the Rainbow Warrior Ill, the Arctic Sunrise and the Witness, further strengthening its capacity to carry out environmental campaigns and scientific research in defense of the environment.

articles.title: U.S. Targets China, EU With New Tariffs Citing Overcapacity
articles.summary: The US announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies under President Donald Trump’s push to restore sweeping global import taxes that the Supreme Court found unconstitutional.
articles.body: Advertise Forum Jobs Subscribe Grab a Seat at the Captain’s Table Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe. Join the leading maritime news network FILE PHOTO: China's President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump visit the Temple of Heaven in Beijing on May 14, 2026. BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/Pool via REUTERS/File Photo By Alicia Diaz (Bloomberg) –The US announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies under President Donald Trump’s push to restore sweeping global import taxes that the Supreme Court found unconstitutional. The rate for imports from China would rise to 20%, in line with the country’s prior agreement with the Trump administration — though that rate could double to 40% if talks between the two countries fall apart, according to a senior US official. The official briefed reporters on condition of anonymity ahead of Wednesday’s announcement. Products from the EU will be taxed at 15% in compliance with the US’s deal with the bloc, though that could also rise to as much as 20%, according to the Office of the US Trade Representative. Tariffs will apply to items from economies the Trump administration accuses of overproduction in some domestic industries and hurting American companies. They are still subject to a public comment process and could change. A final action could come as early as January, the official said. The new levies mark the latest effort by the administration to reinstate an expansive tariff agenda that included country-by-country levies implemented using emergency powers. Those were struck down by high-court justices in February, forcing Trump to invoke other legal authorities to advance his agenda. It’s a politically risky move. Democrats swept to a landslide victory in the midterm elections earlier this month thanks in part to voter anger over the cost of living and disapproval of the president’s handling of the economy. China and the EU could also retaliate, though initial signals from them were muted. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a briefing earlier Wednesday that the prospect of new US tariffs on its exports was “political maneuvering” and said the two nations should work together to maintain their trade truce. The announcement appears to comply with the 2025 trade agreement between the US and EU, which capped tariffs at 15% on most of the bloc’s exports. As a result, the move likely won’t antagonize transatlantic relations for now. European Commission spokesman Olof Gill said “we strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity” and added the bloc expects new levies to abide by the tariff agreement. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the new duties were designed to preserve existing deals while addressing overcapacity concerns. “A lot of these deals we made actually solve a lot of the problems we see in excess capacity or can go toward it,” Greer said Wednesday on CNBC. “We’ve talked to our trading partners about this. They know what we’re proposing. I think a lot of this is baked in.” Imports from Japan, South Korea, Switzerland — all prominent US trading partners — would be hit with a 15% rate. The number could go up to 25% for Korea and 20% for the other two, USTR said. Indian products would face a 17% charge if a trade pact with Washington is finalized, though that could increase to 25%. Several smaller nations in Asia were also hit. Similar expected measures aimed at Mexico and Norway were not included but remain under consideration, the official said. Greer said on CNBC the US has “had some very good conversations with Mexico” on the issue. The tariffs follow a probe that began in March into alleged excess manufacturing capacity, utilizing Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, a process seen as more resistant to legal challenges than Trump’s prior tariff wall. The tariff rates aren’t expected to surpass already agreed-upon levels in trade agreements with each economy. The move will test the tolerance of economic partners, who have largely held back from retaliating, opting instead to negotiate deals with the US to minimize their tariffs. That dynamic could be on display next month, when Trump meets again with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the Group of 20 summit. Their trade truce is set to expire in January unless the two powers agree to extend it. “If we were to go beyond the 20% or something like that, they would view that as breaking our deal,” Greer said, The trade ambassador said Washington and Beijing are also “proposing to implement” tariff reductions under its new board of trade on around $30 billion of non-sensitive exports. Greer signaled that the new levy will not stack on top of existing duties of 10% or 12.5% under a separate investigation into negligent enforcement of forced-labor laws. “Those are not really additive,” he said on CNBC. For products eligible to be hit by both sets of duties, only the higher rate would apply, the official said earlier. The official added that there would be goods exempted from the tariffs, including oil and gas and food products that cannot be grown in the US. Other products that are already subject to sectoral duties, including tariffs on pharmaceuticals and critical minerals, are also exempted. After the Supreme Court loss, Trump immediately announced plans to rebuild his tariff wall under a different legal authority. Under the Section 301 framework, the president can implement tariffs following an investigation into allegedly unfair foreign trading practices. While Section 301 tariffs are seen as more legally sound and flexible than other powers Trump has eyed, they’re also more time-consuming. An earlier investigation under the same legal authority into policies around forced labor from US trading partners resulted in tariffs on some 60 economies. Those duties are currently facing legal challenges. The new tariffs apply to Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam. USTR also announced it is raising tariffs on imports from Brazil, altering a previously-conducted trade investigation into the country’s digital policies and trade practices. The US is considering increasing the out-of-quota tariff rate on raw and refined sugar and proposing a 10% tariff on finished aircraft. Join the leading maritime news network Photo courtesy IMO The International Maritime Organization (IMO) is calling on shipping companies to make more training berths available to cadets, highlighting a longstanding disconnect between the industry’s need for qualified seafarers and the lack of opportunities for young people to gain the sea time required to enter the profession. In many developing countries, aspiring officers complete their shore-based maritime education only to spend years waiting for an onboard training placement, even as shipping companies struggle to recruit qualified personnel. In an announcement Tuesday, the IMO outlined efforts to expand its NextWave Seafarers initiative, which aims to address the bottleneck through cooperation between governments, shipowners and maritime training institutions. More than 80 participants representing over 25 countries gathered at IMO headquarters in London on November 20 to formally launch the second phase of the initiative and explore ways to increase the availability of onboard training opportunities. The program’s pilot phase, developed in partnership with Saudi Arabia’s Transport General Authority and national shipping company Bahri, saw 19 cadets from developing island nations and least developed countries complete their onboard training aboard Bahri vessels. The second phase aims to train at least 30 additional cadets, with women accounting for half of participants. The IMO also wants to recruit at least five shipping companies to provide training berths, laying the groundwork for a wider international partnership. The workshop examined practical barriers to cadet placements, including visa restrictions complicating crew changes, as well as the importance of providing a safe and supportive working environment for young seafarers entering the industry. The shortage of training berths exposes a fundamental challenge in addressing the industry’s workforce needs. Expanding maritime education alone will do little to increase the supply of qualified officers if graduates cannot secure the mandatory sea time needed to earn their professional credentials. Without sufficient participation from shipowners, the industry risks leaving a pool of prospective seafarers untapped at a time when it needs to attract and retain the next generation of maritime professionals. The IMO is encouraging shipping companies and governments interested in supporting the initiative, including by offering training berths, to contact its Technical Cooperation and Implementation Division at [email protected] . articles.summary: Countries bordering the Red Sea and Western Indian Ocean are moving toward establishing a combined maritime task force to combat piracy, strengthen regional security and protect commercial shipping across some...

Join the leading maritime news network An EUNAVFOR warship escorts a CMA CGM containership in the Red Sea as part of the EU's Operation ASPIDES. Photo courtesy EUNAVFOR Countries bordering the Red Sea and Western Indian Ocean are moving toward establishing a combined maritime task force to combat piracy, strengthen regional security and protect commercial shipping across some of the world’s most strategically important waterways. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) announced that signatories to the Djibouti Code of Conduct and its Jeddah Amendment have adopted a new Regional Maritime Security Strategy and agreed to advance plans for a Combined Maritime Task Force (CMTF). The agreement was reached during a high-level meeting held November 11–13 in Antananarivo, Madagascar. The proposed task force would build on existing national and regional maritime security capabilities, improving coordination among participating countries. Governments agreed to develop the force’s legal framework and concept of operations in 2027. The initiative comes amid persistent threats to commercial shipping in the Red Sea and renewed concerns over piracy off the Horn of Africa, underscoring the need for greater regional cooperation in protecting international trade and seafarers. The broader security strategy covers the Western Indian Ocean, Gulf of Aden and Red Sea. Preparatory work began in Saudi Arabia in November 2024, with government representatives, navies, coast guards and maritime law enforcement agencies subsequently meeting in Mombasa, Kenya, earlier this month to finalize the framework. Originally adopted in 2009 in response to Somali piracy, the Djibouti Code of Conduct was expanded in 2017 through the Jeddah Amendment to address a wider range of maritime security threats. Somalia’s Minister of State Mohamed Abdulkadir Mohamed emphasized the human cost of attacks on commercial shipping during the meeting. “The protection of seafarers is not simply a maritime security obligation; it is a fundamental humanitarian responsibility,” he said. The meeting also marked a leadership milestone, with Tanzania’s Stella Katondo becoming the first woman elected to chair the regional initiative. South Africa will serve as deputy chair. While the agreement represents a significant step toward a more coordinated regional security presence, the proposed task force remains in development. The IMO has not announced a deployment timeline or details of participating naval assets. Finnish Border Guard/Handout via REUTERS ROME, Nov 25 (Reuters) – Italy has told Ukraine it was wrong to attack Russian ships in Libyan waters and warned Kyiv not to spread the war to new areas, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Corriere della Sera newspaper on Wednesday. “It was a mistake to violate Libya’s sovereignty,” Tajani said, adding that Rome had received no advance warning of the Ukrainian operations. “Italy was absolutely unaware of Kyiv’s intentions to strike in Libyan territorial waters, even inside a port,” said the minister, who is head of the coalition Forza Italia party. Ukraine has said the maritime drone attack against a Russian naval corvette and a cargo ship at the weekend was a legitimate act of self-defence. Tajani said he had telephoned his Ukrainian counterpart, Andrii Sybiha, to express his concerns, stressing Italy’s commitment to Libya’s territorial integrity. Another coalition party, the far-right League, also condemned the attack, calling it “unacceptable” and warning that it risked destabilising the north African country. Italy has been a staunch supporter of Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion, providing military aid and backing European sanctions against Moscow. However, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has sent mixed signals, with her own party firmly behind Kyiv while the League, led by Matteo Salvini, has repeatedly criticised continued military assistance to Ukraine. Tajani said that Rome would carry on supporting Kyiv’s sovereignty while seeking to prevent the conflict from spreading. “Italy will remain on Ukraine’s side. Ours is a strategic choice,” he said. articles.summary: A record 2,100-plus migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands over 24 hours in overcrowded boats, maritime rescue service data showed on Wednesday, prompting regional leader Fernando Clavijo to call for a European-level response to the crisis."The Canaries can't take it anymore.
articles.body: Canary Islands Receive Recording-Breaking Number of Migrants In Single Day Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 © Adobe Stock/Halina A record 2,100-plus migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands over 24 hours in overcrowded boats, maritime rescue service data showed on Wednesday, prompting regional leader Fernando Clavijo to call for a European-level response to the crisis. "The Canaries can't take it anymore. We're experiencing an unprecedented migration pressure," Clavijo wrote on X, adding that he had requested an urgent meeting with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. "These people come to Europe and it's not fair that we alone respond to a drama of this magnitude," he said. One migrant was found dead in a boat and another gave birth during the perilous crossing from West Africa, the rescue service said. The daily arrivals surpassed the previous record of about 1,500 set two weeks ago. Most of the boats arrived at El Hierro, an island of some 11,400 residents that has become one of Europe's key entry points for migrants from West Africa. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who has faced tough criticism of his open stance on migration during the campaign ahead of Sunday's parliamentary election, said on Wednesday Europe needed a comprehensive approach to migration, including stronger border controls in cooperation with Senegalese and Gambian authorities. Still, he said Spain needed "to open legal migration pathways" for workers in sectors such as housing that are short of qualified labour. The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration crossings as migrants seek to reach Spanish territory despite rough seas, strong currents and long distances. Arrivals tend to pick up in the autumn months, when sea conditions along the route are generally calmer and more favourable for crossings. Arrivals so far this year had climbed to 28,103 as of late November, more than last year's total but still well below an all-time high of 46,843 recorded in 2024, when most crossings occurred during the first nine months of the year. Nearly 21,000 people have reached the archipelago in the last two months. (Reuters)

articles.title: NYK Line, Partners to Advance Remote Ship Emissions Monitoring
articles.summary: Shipping company NYK Line and seven other organizations have signed an agreement to develop remote sensing technology capable of measuring greenhouse gas emissions from vessels without physical contact, with trials focused on Yokohama Port in Japan.The agreement…
articles.body: NYK Line, Partners to Advance Remote Ship Emissions Monitoring Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 Conceptual image of the system (Credit: NYK Line) Shipping company NYK Line and seven other organizations have signed an agreement to develop remote sensing technology capable of measuring greenhouse gas emissions from vessels without physical contact, with trials focused on Yokohama Port in Japan. The agreement, signed on November 25, brings together NYK Line, MUFG Bank, Nagoya Electric Works, ArkEdge Space, Shimizu Corporation, the City of Yokohama, Yokohama-Kawasaki International Port Corporation and Yokohama Port Corporation. The collaboration will advance the True Emission Eye - Maritime project, which aims to develop technology for measuring, visualizing and quantifying greenhouse gas emissions from ships at a distance. The project will conduct measurements on actual vessels at Yokohama Port to assess the technology's accuracy, while examining system specifications, potential applications and opportunities for future commercial deployment. The technology is being developed to complement existing methods of estimating vessel emissions based on fuel type and consumption, providing a means of directly measuring emissions from outside ships. The system uses optical observation technology that exploits the ability of gases, including carbon dioxide, to absorb and emit light at specific wavelengths. Data obtained from vessel exhaust observations is combined with physical parameters, including distance to the ship and weather conditions, to calculate emissions. Testing has already been conducted at experimental facilities and on NYK Group vessels, both at berth and underway. At Yokohama Port, the project has captured infrared images of ship exhaust from observation points including Osanbashi Pier and the Yokohama Bay Bridge Skywalk. The images are being compared and analyzed against vessel data to evaluate the technology. The partners will continue conducting measurements under different conditions to improve the accuracy of the system, while also examining fixed-point monitoring at ports. The project will also assess the technical requirements for satellite-based observations of ship emissions and explore the potential integration of satellite measurements with ground-based data. The eight organizations aim to bring the technology into practical use to improve transparency in vessel emissions reporting and support decarbonization across the shipping and port sectors.

articles.summary: A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated.

Join the leading maritime news network Photo: Avigator Thailand/Shutterstock By Weilun Soon Nov 25, 2026 (Bloomberg) –A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated. Less than a quarter of the world’s 542 long-range 2, or LR2, tankers are currently transporting “clean” cargoes such as jet fuel, naphtha and diesel as of this week, according to Signal Ocean data. The vessels have cargo holds that are coated to transport refined fuels, and have to undergo an expensive cleaning process to return to the trade once they ship “dirty” crude oil. The shift in use of the LR2 fleet comes as crude flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz. A system of shuttling tankers and ship-to-ship transfers has helped exports from the Persian Gulf recover to pre-war levels, boosting freight rates and prompting charterers to tap smaller vessels to meet demand. Benchmark earnings for very-large crude carriers have soared, in turn enabling smaller-sized tankers — including Aframaxes, which are the crude-focused equivalent of LR2s, able to hold about 750,000 barrels — to command far higher fees. And an LR2 that dirties up can charge Aframax earnings. Shipping executives often look at how many LR2s are switching to plan on how much they can charge, and how they should deploy their tankers around the world. Even though the LR2 fleet has grown 12% since January last year and clean-fuel shipments have fallen due to the US-Iran war, the increased switching to crude has helped put a floor underneath the fees they can command to carry oil products. “Tracking LR2 employment between clean and dirty trades is becoming as important as monitoring the size of the fleet itself,” Signal analysts Maria Bertzeletou and Georgios Sakellariou said. The switching of LR2s started last year as traders sought to store more crude on vessels at sea, but accelerated in the initial phase of the Iran War from the end of February, when refineries in the Middle East were attacked by the Islamic Republic — reducing the need for clean tankers, Sakellariou said. Read More: Oil Tankers Get ‘Dirty’ Ditching Fuels for Crude as Rates Boom A lot of the processing plants in the region remain unavailable, reducing the need for products tankers. About 1.7 million out of the more than 9 million barrels a day of refining capacity is currently offline in the Middle East, RBC Capital Markets analysts including Christopher Louney and Helima Croft wrote in a note this week. Around 1 million barrels a day of that potentially needs months to repair, they said. Charterers are turning to smaller product tankers, with the share of LR2s in transporting fuels falling to just 12% between July and September, from almost 18% a year earlier, Signal data show. Meanwhile, a benchmark freight index reflecting daily LR2 earnings from the Mediterranean to Asia increased more than five-fold, while another from the Middle East to Europe jumped more than 10-fold in the year through end-September. © 2026 Bloomberg L.P. Join the leading maritime news network On 24 November 2026, Windcat signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for the second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) in the Innovation Series. The contract follows the order for the first vessel , with an option for five more, signed in November last year. Sound basis The MP-ASV is an entirely new type of vessel designed to support operations in the offshore energy industry . Its design draws heavily on Damen’s experience in the design and construction of Commissioning Services Operations Vessels (CSOVs). This includes the Elevation Series CSOVs, developed together by Damen and Windcat. The first vessel in the Elevation Series, Windcat Rotterdam , was presented with the KNVTS Ship of the Year Award at this year’s Maritime Awards Gala. The MP-ASV takes the proven capabilities of the Elevation Series CSOVs and builds on them further. Extended capabilities The MP-ASVs build on these capabilities in a number of ways, including with their 102 x 20 metre hull and its 750m 2 deck space. The MP-ASV is able to assist and operate in all offshore energy markets, including cable repair, flotel functions, offshore wind and ROV assistance. Additionally, the vessel is fitted with 111 cabins, allowing up to 190 persons on board. The vessel features an offshore crane which can be used as a 150-tonne subsea crane, or as a 15-tonne 3D motion-compensated crane. The vessel can also be fitted with remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). The vessels are being equipped with a DP2+ system holding DNV CBS and CBT class notations, which cover a wider scope of redundant closed bus-ties system arrangements, for enhanced fault tolerance. The DP system features additional tunnel thrusters fore and aft to provide increased redundancy for safe operations in remote offshore locations. Access is via a 3D motion-compensated gangway with two exchangeable tips, one for short connections used in the wind industry and one capable of long continuous connections. Prepared for efficiency The MP-ASVs will be outfitted with a battery system to enable peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing. This will enable highly efficient operations, for example when in DP mode. Like the Windcat CSOVs, a key feature of the Innovation Series vessels is the integration of low-carbon fuels . Hence a dual fuel hydrogen auxiliary genset is installed, and the three main generator sets are of the next generation Evolve generator sets from ABC, which allow for a range of low-emission possibilities. These engines can operate on liquid fuels such as biodiesel and HVO, on dual fuel with pilot injection of liquid fuel, or on 100% gas using spark ignition. High offshore comfort level The design of the vessel is also highly focused on comfort for the up to 190 personnel onboard. Measures include well-thought-out routing, use of high-quality materials and aesthetically appealing accommodation. The aim is to make crew and personnel feel at home during extended periods of up to 150 days offshore, due to her extended fuel capacity. Strength-to-strength Damen Sales Director Joost van der Weiden says, “We are delighted to receive this second MP-ASV order from Windcat. The cooperation that began with our development of the Elevation Series continues to grow in strength. With the Innovation Series we mutually have developed a vessel that will further enhance Windcat’s capabilities to support its clients in the offshore energy industry in the years ahead.” Windcat Managing Director Willem van der Wel says: “The decision to order a second MP-ASV reflects our confidence in this new vessel concept and our ambition to further strengthen our position in the offshore energy market. By combining the capabilities of a multi-purpose support vessel with high-quality offshore accommodation, we are creating a versatile solution that responds to the evolving needs of our customers. articles.body: Petronas Names ‘World's First’ Nearshore FLNG Facility Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Petronas) Petronas has officially named its third floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility, PFLNG TIGA, at Samsung Heavy Industries' shipyard in South Korea, ahead of its planned deployment to Malaysia and start-up in the third quarter of 2027. Described by Petronas as the world's first nearshore FLNG facility, PFLNG TIGA is currently under construction at the shipyard on Geoje Island and will be deployed to Sipitang, Sabah, Malaysia. The facility is designed to produce 2 million tonnes of LNG annually and measures 281 metres in length, 64 metres in width and 32 metres in depth. PFLNG TIGA will become the third floating LNG facility developed by Petronas , expanding its portfolio of facilities designed for shallow-water, deepwater and nearshore environments. The new facility is intended to support the development and commercialisation of gas resources while strengthening Malaysia's LNG supply capabilities. Petronas said the addition would provide greater flexibility in bringing gas resources to market and meeting regional and international demand. The company has been active in the LNG industry for more than four decades, with PFLNG TIGA representing another addition to its integrated LNG portfolio.

articles.body: Oil Falls as Supply Glut Concerns Overshadow Hormuz Shipping Risks Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 © Miha Creative / Adobe Stock Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East. Brent crude futures LCOc1 declined 44 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.96 a barrel at 1035 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures CLc1 slipped 62 cents, or 0.8%, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday. "Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand," said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage. On Wednesday, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery ‌and Riyadh's financial district. Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, is part of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast ‌that ⁠also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude. A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to the softer oil prices, Varga said. US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. API/S Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average. "Uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies in the upcoming November 29 meeting, especially with the UAE no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies and Iraq seeking higher oil output capacity, as well as broader market risk-off are some reasons," said Zhenqiang Seto, a senior research specialist for oil at LSEG. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy. "Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno said. Iraq is pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening tensions over a review that will help determine how much members can pump next year. Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has also reopened after an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya. "However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges of attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," Ueno said. A container ship was targeted and came to a stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media. On Monday, three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles as they sailed east through the strait, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday. articles.body: Windcat Expands Offshore Fleet with Second Damen Multi-Purpose Vessel Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Windcat) Windcat has signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for a second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) under its Innovation Series, expanding its planned fleet of vessels designed for offshore energy operations. The agreement, signed on November 24, follows Windcat's initial order in November 2025 for the first vessel in the series, which included an option for five additional units. The new MP-ASV design builds on the companies' earlier collaboration on the Elevation Series commissioning service operations vessels (CSOVs), incorporating additional capabilities for offshore wind, subsea cable repair, offshore accommodation and remotely operated vehicle (ROV) support. The vessels will measure 102 meters in length and 20 meters in width, with approximately 750 square meters of deck space and 111 cabins accommodating up to 190 personnel. Each MP-ASV will feature an offshore crane capable of operating as a 150-tonne subsea crane or a 15-tonne three-dimensional motion-compensated crane, alongside provisions for ROV installation. Personnel transfers will be supported by a 3D motion-compensated gangway with interchangeable tips designed for short connections in offshore wind operations and longer continuous connections. The vessels will also feature a DP2+ dynamic positioning system with DNV CBS and CBT class notations, incorporating additional bow and stern tunnel thrusters to improve redundancy during offshore operations. The propulsion and power arrangement will include a battery system for peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing, together with a dual-fuel hydrogen auxiliary generator. Three main generator sets supplied by ABC will feature its Evolve technology, designed to accommodate different fuel options, including biodiesel, hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), dual-fuel operation and gas. The MP-ASVs are designed for extended offshore deployments of up to 150 days, supported by increased fuel capacity and accommodation facilities intended for prolonged stays at sea. The Innovation Series builds on Damen and Windcat's Elevation Series partnership, which includes the Windcat Rotterdam, named KNVTS Ship of the Year at the 2026 Maritime Awards Gala.
